exhibits.title: Beer — the Beverage that Heals Labor
exhibits.thesis: Beer read as the dream that soothes labour, forking from one ancient stem. Born of the gods in Mesopotamia and made a wage in Egypt, brewing is kept alive by the medieval monasteries — then the modern age splits it in two: ALE, the warm-fermented soul of the Benelux abbeys, England's porter, and Poland's smoked grodziskie; and LAGER, the cold-fermented clarity of Vienna and Bavaria. Two rivers of the worker's cup, from one barley spring.

exhibits.title: The Dream of Print
exhibits.thesis: The dream of multiplying the written word, read as a fork from one root. From East Asian woodblock the craft branches: West, it turns to metal — movable type and the copperplate meeting in Gutenberg's press, through publishing and the steam press to offset, and text becomes everyone's; East, the block stays a block, crosses to Japan as the people's ukiyo-e, and through Japonisme reshapes Art Nouveau — the birth of commercial design. Two dreams of the multiplied image, from one carved page.

exhibits.title: The Wish to Fly — Icarus's Wings
exhibits.thesis: The dream of flight read as a genealogy of falls and flights: myth foreshadows history, and each rise carries its fall.
